name: keys loses the key union
code:
const levels = { off: 0, warn: 1 };
export const names = Object.keys(levels);

name: entries loses it in the first position
code:
const levels = { off: 0, warn: 1 };
export const pairs = Object.entries(levels);

name: values keeps the value type
code:
const levels = { off: 0, warn: 1 };
export const numbers = Object.values(levels);

name: a count reads no key
code:
const levels = { off: 0, warn: 1 };
export const empty = Object.keys(levels).length === 0;

name: a count on entries is the same case
code:
const levels = { off: 0, warn: 1 };
export const size = Object.entries(levels).length;

name: a mapped result still reads the keys
code:
const levels = { off: 0, warn: 1 };
export const upper = Object.keys(levels).map((key) => key.toUpperCase());

name: a shadowed Object is not the global
an imported Object is not the global
code:
import Object from "custom";

export const names = Object.keys({ off: 0 });

name: the helper names come from the options
code:
const levels = { off: 0, warn: 1 };
export const names = Object.keys(levels);

name: a computed access names the method too
code:
const levels = { off: 0, warn: 1 };
export const names = Object["keys"](levels);

name: a destructured declaration above the call is not the helper
code:
const levels = { off: 0, warn: 1 };
export const { names } = { names: Object.keys(levels) };

name: a computed method name above the call is not the helper
